public_rationale: Microsoft's archived July 2024 release notes describe spreadsheet functions, including conditional formatting, but provide no measured success rate or correction burden [e1]. A report published in July 2024 describes increased document activity among Copilot users while explicitly stating that its telemetry does not directly measure productivity or output quality [e2]. These items do not establish whether July 2024 systems meaningfully completed routine work beyond assistance, or provided the described broadly personalized assistance [e1, e2]. They also do not establish that systems were unable to do so [e1, e2].
limitations: The supplied office-work evidence comes from Microsoft.
Feature descriptions and activity counts do not measure verified task completion, quality or total human effort.
The packet lacks adequate evaluation of broadly personalized assistance.

our_interpretation: The claim concerns practical capabilities available around publication, not later products.
For this ongoing state with no reporting cycle, the target is July 2024, the latest completed calendar month before the post.
The ordinary reading concerns meaningful completion of routine work and broadly useful personalized assistance. It does not require literal omniscience or flawless performance.
The surrounding passage expressly allows speeding up processes in existing systems. Such assistance alone does not settle whether drudgery was automated away.
criteria.support_condition: Representative testing of then-available systems establishes that they cannot meaningfully complete routine spreadsheet or document work or provide the described broadly personalized assistance.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Contemporaneous, reproducible demonstrations or deployments establish meaningful completion of routine work beyond mere acceleration, or the described broadly personalized assistance.
